messages:
Mina: quick follow-up from the AttrV2 RFCwe've been converging on cost_claim sentinels, but folks raised a subtle correctness vs latency tradeoff: do we require claims to be strongly ordered/atomic with the enriched envelope, or accept weaker guarantees and correct later? want to get a principled ops pattern.
Owen: tl;dr: strong atomicity gives correctness but adds latency and coupling. weaker eventual claims are faster but require compensating logic for billing. we should list options and their failure modes.
Luis: option A: synchronous enrichment+claim commit 12PC-like behavior between enrichment and billing write. pro: billing always sees cost_key; con: high tail latency and dependence on billing availability.
Rhea: option B: fire-and-forget claim with monotonic versioning: enrichment writes envelope (maybe sampled) then emits claim record with claim_version. billing uses the highest seen version per trace. pro: low latency; con: needs robust idempotency and a correction lane for late higher-version claims.
Mina: option C: optimistic in-ingest attribution: if envelope lacks cost_key, mark provisional_cost=unknown and run billing with a provisional bucket. when a claim arrives, emit a correction transaction that reassigns tokens. cheaper reads but requires backfill/compensation and auditing.
Owen: failure modes: network partitions -> claims delayed -> tokens misbilled; duplicate claims -> double-reassignment risk; out-of-order claims -> need versioning. mitigation: every claim carries claim_version+origin and we require monotonic compare.
Luis: practical compromise: adopt option B with small additions: 1) claim_version (int) and claim_ts on every claim 2) a compact, strongly-consistent index for latest claim per trace with TTL (7d) using a consensus-backed store (raft/etcd) for small footprint keys, not full envelopes 3) correction stream that is appended when claim_version increases after billing checkpoint.
Rhea: how do we bound the correction work? we need to avoid scanning large token sets for each correction. proposal: bucket claims by billing-window id (date+hour) and store counts per bucket on claim write. when a correction arrives, we enqueue a bucket-level re-aggregation job limited by cost budget. also expose a "corrections_pending" gauge per org.
Mina: good. and for idempotency: claims are write-if-newer semantics keyed by trace_digest (sha256 truncated). store (trace_digest -> {claim_version, cost_key, claim_ts, origin}). writes are idempotent and concurrent-safe.
Owen: operationally we must instrument: claim_latency_p95, claim_version_increase_rate, corrections_pending, provisional_billed_tokens_ratio. set alert if corrections_pending > X or provisional_billed_tokens_ratio > 0.25%.
Luis: SDK/backwards compat: continue dual-write for V1+V2 during migration. also emit legacy_key_metric so owners can nudge clients. server-side translation table still useful for 6-12 months.
Rhea: data model note: keep CORE columns small and typed. store cost_claim_status in core with values: ingress, enrichment, provisional, corrected, missing. this helps query and SLO dashboards.
Mina: rollout steps: 1) implement claim-index prototype in a small raft-backed KV (store just trace_digest->claim metadata), 2) enrichment emits claim with claim_version and optional estimated_bucket_hint, 3) billing consults claim-index at join; if absent mark provisional and emit provisional metric, 4) correction processor listens to claim changelog and enqueues bounded re-aggregations. start 3% dual-write canary for 2w, measure corrections rate and latency.
Owen: owners: Mina = rollout doc + claim-index prototype, Luis = correction processor + bounded re-agg runner, Rhea = dashboard/alerts + schema defs. i'll wire up infra ticket.
ingest-bot: created follow-up ticket ORG-11456 "AttrV2: versioned claims + bounded corrections" assigned to Mina, Luis, Rhea. :white_check_mark:
Mina: thanks, will post the addendum RFC link once it's live.
